name: Washing clothes properly

lead: This covers ordinary laundry practice: detergent, agitation, rinsing and drying. People interested in smelling clean often examine it.
The general reference used here does not address odour specifically.

paras: Detergent surfactants lift dirt, agitation loosens it and rinsing removes it; temperature affects chemical activity and fabric shrinkage.
Wikipedia notes heat and agitation can shrink wool and hot water can cause colour loss, so care labels matter.[1]

lead: Washing clothes properly is a grooming practice concerned with cleaning garments so that odour, dirt and stains are removed and fabrics last.[1] In appearance communities it is raised mainly in connection with clothing that retains smell.

Laundry typically involves washing with detergent, agitation, rinsing and drying; Wikipedia notes that warmer water increases chemical activity and stain solubility, while heat and agitation can shrink wool and cold water reduces colour bleeding.[1] The article does not discuss odour specifically.

paras: Surfactants in detergent mobilise dirt, agitation loosens it, and rinsing carries it out of the fibres.[1] Many guides advise washing whites separately from colours, and care symbols indicate how each garment should be treated.[1]

Wikipedia says cotton is washed cooler to avoid shrinkage. It also reports that drying at 60 degrees Celsius or higher for thirty minutes kills many parasites such as dust mites, and that three hours of direct sunlight kills mite eggs.[1]
